doc.title: Norris Turney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

chapter: Back in Ohio, Philadelphia and the 1950s
title: Going home, regretting California, group in Ohio, New York and Philadelphia
summary: He left the road bands, regretting missing California, led a group in Ohio, then lived in New York and about six years in Philadelphia, playing with Elmer Snowden.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So you moved back to Ohio.
Yeah, after I leave these bands I went back home.
Enough of this bus stuff, huh?
Yeah. I’m sorry I left, because they were on their way to California. I’d never been to California before. So I regret that to this day.
What happened when you got back home?

Well I got a little group together, worked around Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana. And then I went back to New York, I guess about 19— 50s, in the 50s. Yeah, early 50s I’d say. I had a group around New York for a while, and as a matter of fact I went from New York to Philadelphia, and I lived in Philadelphia about six years, and played with Elmer Snowden.
